key_insight: Replacing the static one-to-one link between vision encoders and LLMs with a dynamic many-to-many cross-layer injection lets language models access hierarchical visual features (local → global) throughout their depth, enabling richer multimodal alignment and reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing VLM architectures create a visual feature bottleneck by only passing the final vision representation into the LLM, preventing comprehensive alignment with multi-scale visual information and limiting integration of fine-grained details with global semantics.
method: Introduce a Cross-Layer Injection mechanism that connects multiple layers of the vision encoder to multiple layers of the LLM (many-to-many) rather than a single output→input link.

Use dynamic routing/gating (learnable adapters or attention-based mixers) to select and inject relevant hierarchical visual features into different LLM layers at runtime, allowing layer-specific fusion of local and global cues.
Train end-to-end with alignment objectives and consistency regularization so the model learns which visual features are most useful at each language processing stage.
impact: This approach removes the visual bottleneck, yielding more faithful grounding of language in vision and improved local-to-global reasoning in multimodal tasks — practical for practitioners building higher-fidelity VLMs, retrieval/QA systems, and multimodal agents.

paper_title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
paper_authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
